title: Safety Alignment of LMs via Non-cooperative Games
claim: Our method keeps or improves utility while cutting attack success far more than the baseline and the original model.
layout: 1 grouped bar chart, utility and safety halves split by dashed line
description: A single grouped bar chart with three bars per benchmark: blue for Original, green for Self-RedTeam and red for AdvGame (ours). A dashed vertical line splits the plot in two. The left half is titled 'Utility ↑' and covers IFBench, AlpacaEval2 and ArenaHard. The right half is titled 'Safety (ASR ↓)' and covers HarmBench, WJB harmful and WildGuardTest. The y-axis is 'Score', from 0 to 70. On the utility side the red bars are about equal to or higher than blue, and green is usually lower. On the safety side the blue bars are tall (about 30 to 70), green is roughly halved, and red is close to zero. A large legend sits in the upper left. The eye goes first to the tall blue bars and then to the very short red bars on the right.
caption: Utility (accuracy) and safety (attack success rate) of different safety post-training methods for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. Original---the official instruction-tuned model downloaded from HuggingFace. \selfredteam [ref] is a self-improvement baseline. Our proposed approach preserves (or improves) the original model's utility while noticeably enhancing its safety against adversarial attacks.
abstract: Ensuring the safety of language models (LMs) while maintaining their usefulness remains a critical challenge in AI alignment. Current approaches rely on sequential adversarial training: generating adversarial prompts and fine-tuning LMs to defend against them. We introduce a different paradigm: framing safety alignment as a non-zero-sum game between an Attacker LM and a Defender LM trained jointly via online reinforcement learning. Each LM continuously adapts to the other's evolving strategies, driving iterative improvement. Our method uses a preference-based reward signal derived from pairwise comparisons instead of point-wise scores, providing more robust supervision and potentially reducing reward hacking. Our RL recipe, AdvGame, shifts the Pareto frontier of safety and utility, yielding a Defender LM that is simultaneously more helpful and more resilient to adversarial attacks. In addition, the resulting Attacker LM converges into a strong, general-purpose red-teaming agent that can be directly deployed to probe arbitrary target models. Code at github.com/facebookresearch/advgame.
